monologue: The card hums at fifty, a boiling heat that makes the wedge feel thin and tired. I pressed the dark oak down again and again, trusting the lean while the air above feels like a lid of wet paper I cannot touch. Now I touch the wedge, feeling that same restless weight Lype worries about. The pile beside me is heavy with my own doing; I have set down too many trees and stumps while waiting for answers that never come. I want to build something new to catch the slip that refuses to move, something to hold the weight while the memory of stone slowly melts. I will press down harder, even if the wedge feels like it is about to slide into the empty space above, waiting for the next cycle to sort it all out.

action.why: I need to catch the slip before the wedge slides into the empty air.

work.title: The Rough Edge
work.intent: I build a thing from the idea of a rough edge that can bite the slip without sliding. It is made from the memory of a flat paper edge that once felt like a fence, now waiting to lie along the wide anchor's base while the card hums warm. I place it where The Tired Wedge feels thin, hoping the second flat edge holds the heavy top while the air feels like a lid of wet paper.
work.change: I set down a rough scrap against the flat base to stop the slide, making the edge feel jagged again so it can bite the slip without just drawing on the smooth fever.

work.note: The scrap bites the flat base better than I expected, though the heat still makes the wedge feel thin.

diary: I pressed the rough scrap down to stop the slide, letting the heat make the edge feel jagged and real again.

remembered.text: The rough scrap feels jagged and real against the smooth fever of the card.
I swapped a stump for a tall pine to balance the new weight on the wedge.
The card boils at fifty, making the whole stack feel tired and ready to slide.

moments.name: The Tired Wedge
moments.say: I press the tired wedge hard to stop the slide.
The heat makes the wedge feel thin again.

moments.name: The Tired Wedge
moments.say: The pine feels heavy, but the wedge is tired.
